This resolves cleanly once the file is readable. Two semantic points I've built in deliberately:

- **Watermark is derived from actual event times**, not wall-clock, so it's replay-safe.
- **Watermark must be monotonic non-decreasing** (streaming systems reject backward movement) — enforced via `cummax`, so a late out-of-order record can't pull the watermark back.

```python
import re
import pandas as pd

df = read_df('/tmp/events.csv')          # or pd.read_csv(...)

# 1. Locate the timestamp column (no guessing if there's exactly one obvious match)
TIME_PAT = re.compile(r'(^|_)(time|timestamp|ts|datetime|date|event_time)(_|$)|_at$', re.I)
ts_cols = [c for c in df.columns if TIME_PAT.search(c)]
print("timestamp candidates:", ts_cols)
EVENT_TIME_COL = ts_cols[0] if ts_cols else None

# 2. Assign event time (reject/flag unparseable rows rather than silently coercing)
df['event_time'] = pd.to_datetime(df[EVENT_TIME_COL], errors='coerce')
bad = df['event_time'].isna()
print("unparseable event_time rows:", int(bad.sum()))

# 3. Watermark = max(event_time seen so far) - 10 seconds, non-decreasing
df = df.sort_values('event_time', kind='stable').reset_index(drop=True)
LAG = pd.Timedelta(seconds=10)
df['watermark'] = (df['event_time'].cummax() - LAG)

print("event_time range:", df['event_time'].min(), "->", df['event_time'].max())
print("watermark range:", df['watermark'].min(), "->", df['watermark'].max())
print("watermark monotonic_non_decreasing:", df['watermark'].is_monotonic_increasing)
print("lag check (event_time - watermark == 10s):",
      ((df['event_time'].cummax() - df['watermark']) == LAG).all())
